$comment: The command manifest of FileDO (APP-COMMANDS 0.3 rule 18). filedo.exe is the front of every user verb; the running filedo_win.exe (main window, Disk Manager, tray) is the first instance that answers over its command pipe. filedo.exe and filedo_win.exe each embed this exact file and a test holds them equal (APP-COMMANDS case C1). Aliases are objects naming spelling, exe, legacy and (for fire-and-forget start spellings) answers: false. Non-forwarded console grammars (target-first, fdsec, vd) are listed in families[] and keep their own exit and event contracts (APP-COMMANDS rule 11, item B). Verbs with forward: never run in the receiving process without touching the pipe or first instance; developer tooling verbs carry audience: developer and exe: filedo_win.exe.

families.name: target-first
families.summary: Target-first device, folder, file, share and batch operations (info, speed, test, fill, clean, cd, copy, compare, check, wipe, backup, restore, from, hist).

families.name: vd
families.summary: Virtual disks (.fdd containers and FileDO GPT partitions, 31 verbs).

commands.name: commands
commands.summary: Print the list of commands this product accepts.

args.name: developer
args.description: Include developer tooling verbs in the readable list.

args.name: json
args.description: Print the manifest itself as JSON.

exit 0; one line per user command with its summary and the console families
exit 0; user commands, developer tools and the console families

exitCodes.meaning: the running copy is elevated and this caller is not

commands.name: quit
commands.summary: Close the running window program cleanly; with none running there is nothing to do. A run in progress makes it refuse, unless --stop-jobs stops the runs first.

args.name: stop-jobs
args.description: Stop the runs in progress gracefully, as the Stop button does, wait for them to end and then close. Without it a run in progress makes quit refuse, because the window's own Exit would ask the person.

exitCodes.meaning: no answer within the bound, or with --stop-jobs a run did not end within it; the program is left open and the runs keep the stop that was asked
a run is in progress and --stop-jobs was not given, or the window program is busy
the running copy is elevated and this caller is not

examples.expect: exit 0 (errorlevel 0) when nothing runs
0 once the program closed, 11 while a run is in progress
0 after the runs stopped and the program closed

commands.name: job list
commands.summary: List the runs in progress in the main window and the Disk Manager, and the operations waiting in the Disk Manager's queue.

returns.name: jobs
returns.description: one object per run: where (shell or manager), verb (the console verb of the run), state (running or queued), step (the name of the run's current step, empty when it has not named one) and percent (a whole number, null when the run has not said how much there is to do); no path and no name of the person's files; an empty array when nothing runs

exitCodes.meaning: the running copy is elevated and this caller is not

examples.expect: the number of runs and queued operations; exit 11 when the window program is not running
exit 0; one line per run with where, verb, state, step and percent, or a sentence saying nothing runs

commands.name: job stop
commands.summary: Ask the runs in progress to stop gracefully, as the Stop button does, empty the Disk Manager's queue and wait until no run of that window is left.

args.name: where
args.description: Which window's runs to stop and wait for: shell is the main window (the Job page and the Command page), manager is the Disk Manager.

returns.name: stopped
returns.description: runs that were asked to stop; 0 when nothing ran

returns.name: cleared
returns.description: queued operations taken out of the Disk Manager's queue; 0 when the queue was empty

exitCodes.meaning: no run of that window is left, or none was running
a run did not end within the bound; the stop it was asked for stays requested and no run is ended by force
the running copy is elevated and this caller is not

examples.expect: exit 0 once no run is left
the number of runs of the Disk Manager that were asked to stop
